newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares fall, big gains not seen.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares fall, big gains not seen.

text.p: Shares declined and turnover remained at a low 367,000 litas on Lithunia's stock exchange Monday, as brokers said they expected no serious turn around until autumn.
"The market is very pessimistic," said Kestutis Kupshys, a broker with Mendes Prior Europe.
The index of the official list of shares fell 14.74 points to 878.74 points, while group A shares declined 8.56 points to 1907.02 points.
"The main thing now is that the market is not getting active, but there is much less supply at this level," said Tomas Andrejauskas, a broker with Suprema.

"At these price levels, there will be a very small supply and the prices will go up this week or next by two, three or five percent, but not more," Andrejauskas said. "A more active market we expect at the end of the summer."
Rokishkis Cheese dominated block trades, with 2.3 million litas turnover at a price range of 40 litas to 45 litas.
Total block trade turnover was 2.5 million litas, compared to 197,000 litas Friday.
Rokishkis traded at 43.47 litas on the central market, with a turnover of 75,000 litas.
Rokishkis Cheese said on Monday that shareholders had approved a proposal to issue 200,000 new shares with a face value of ten litas.
The shareholders decided that the minimum price for the shares would be 44.00 litas and that the current shareholders would have no priority rights to buy into the issue.
